validity.recommendation: none — existence, classification, ownership, and start-year all check out against independent regulator and trade-press sources; see the two concern entries below for value-level fixes
validity.researcher_notes: Existence and classification confirmed independently of GEM/gem.wiki: FERC Docket CP00-6 (certificated 2001, NGI trade-press coverage), FERC Docket CP19-475-000 (Phase VI expansion, Federal Register notice 2019-06-21 + PHMSA special-permit notice Federal Register 2019-07-29), and the operator's own site (gulfstreamgas.com, owned by Williams+Enbridge) all independently describe the same 745-mile interstate gas transmission line from Mississippi/Alabama across the Gulf of Mexico to Florida, in service since June 2002. This is a real, correctly-classified interstate transmission pipeline (Fuel=Gas correct), not a phantom or a gathering/process line, and does not duplicate any other roster PID (no other Gulfstream-named row in the 50-row roster; Sabal Trail P0249, Southeast Supply Header P0164, and Florida Gas Transmission P2529/P2594/P2627/P2733/P2738/P4028-40/P4050/P4060 are physically distinct systems per FERC docket and operator identity). Owner1=Williams Companies/Owner2=Enbridge (50/50) confirmed by gulfstreamgas.com/about/sponsors/ (operator's own ownership page, current) and by Wikipedia's short article (independent, 'owned by Enbridge and Williams'); historically Spectra Energy held the Enbridge share pre-2017 merger (hydrocarbons-technology.com 2012 dates it 'Williams (50%), Spectra Energy (50%)') — consistent lineage, not a conflict. Status=operating confirmed (operator's own current Fast Facts page, live system with 6 in-service phases through Phase VI in July 2022). StartYear1=2002 confirmed at high tier by THREE independent sources: hydrocarbons-technology.com ('Commercial Operations Started June 2002'), gulfstreamgas.com Fast Facts ('Phase I in-service May 28, 2002'), and the operator's own Oct. 2, 2001 press release ('scheduled June 2002 in-service date'). Length=1199 km confirmed at high tier: hydrocarbons-technology.com states 745 miles/1,198 km, gulfstreamgas.com Fast Facts states 745 miles (breakdown: 294 mi FL onshore, 15 mi AL/MS, 17 mi offshore processing, 419 mi offshore to FL) — both independent of each other and of GEM, both essentially match the sheet's 1199 km (745 mi = ~1199 km) within normal rounding. Note the pipeline's own 2001-era press materials cited 753 miles (Oct 2001 construction-progress release) and NGI's 2001 coverage cited 744 miles — both slightly higher than the current as-built 745 mi figure; this is a normal planned-vs-as-built drift, not a material discrepancy, and current sources (hydrocarbons-technology + gulfstreamgas Fast Facts) agree with the sheet. Opened and read to exhaustion: gem.wiki page (background section), gulfstreamgas.com (Fast Facts, Ownership, Phase VI, sponsors pages), hydrocarbons-technology.com project page, the 2019-06-21 and 2019-07-29 Federal Register notices, the operator's 2001-10-02 press release PDF, FundingUniverse's Coastal Corporation company history, and NGI's 2001-02-26 'It's a Go' article — 9 of the row's harvested/independently-found documents opened in full; hydrocarbons-technology.com and Wikipedia were both cited already in gem.wiki's own reference list and were verified live and re-read for every column they touch (rule 4b, read to exhaustion).

validity.recommendation: add Mississippi to StartState/Province (or otherwise record the true multi-state origin) — the sheet's 'Mobile County, Alabama' start point is where the line is compressed, not where it originates
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Location [ref] unit has StartLocation='Mobile County', StartState/Province='Alabama' only (EndState/Province='Florida' is fine). THREE independent sources disagree with treating Alabama as the sole/primary origin: (1) Wikipedia's article states the line 'brings gas from Mississippi and Alabama...to Florida' — Mississippi named first; (2) hydrocarbons-technology.com states 'The pipeline originates from a gas gathering system in Mississippi and terminates in Coden, a coastal fishing village in southern Mobile County, Alabama. Here, the gas is compressed at compressor station (CS) 410' — i.e. Mobile County AL is a compression/receipt point mid-route, not the true upstream origin, which is a Mississippi gas-gathering system; (3) FERC's 2019-06-21 Federal Register notice for the Phase VI expansion independently states the added capacity runs 'from existing points of receipt in Mississippi and Alabama to an existing point of delivery in Manatee County, Florida' — a regulator document, naming both states as receipt points. gem.wiki itself (read for leads only, not cited) also says 'runs from Mississippi and Alabama.' All of this matches the scope note's flagged route-vs-sheet disagreement for this row. The EndLocation cell is also blank; independent sources place the Gulf landfall at Port Manatee/Manatee County, FL, with the line continuing onshore through Polk and Martin counties to a terminus in Pinellas County (hydrocarbons-technology.com) — a more precise EndLocation than the sheet currently records. Recommend Update route the StartState/Province fix (add Mississippi) and consider a more specific EndLocation (Manatee County / Pinellas County, FL) sourced the same way.

validity.recommendation: update Capacity — sheet's 1310.00 MMcf/d looks like a pre-Phase-VI figure; current operator-stated capacity is 1,378 MMcf/d (1.378 Bcf/d)
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet records Capacity=1310.00 MMcf/d (LastUpdated 2022-10-11). gem.wiki attributes 1.31 Bcf/d to its 'Wikipedia' citation, but the actual Wikipedia article (verified live, read in full) is a two-sentence stub that states no capacity figure at all — that lineage does not hold up. Independent sources instead show: hydrocarbons-technology.com (2012 vintage, i.e. pre-Phase-VI) states 1.29 Bcf/d = 1290 MMcf/d; the operator's own CURRENT Fast Facts page (gulfstreamgas.com, live 2026) states 'Capacity: 1.378 billion cubic feet per day' = 1378 MMcf/d, and explicitly logs 'Phase VI in-service July 2022' as the most recent capacity addition. FERC's Phase VI docket (CP19-475-000; Federal Register 2019-06-21 and PHMSA special-permit notice 2019-07-29) independently corroborates a +78,000 dekatherms/day (~75-78 MMcf/d) firm-capacity addition that went in-service July 2022 (per gulfstreamgas.com/phase-vi/, 'completed and went in-service in July of 2022') — arithmetically consistent with capacity rising from ~1300 pre-Phase-VI to 1378 post-Phase-VI. Since Phase VI's in-service date (July 2022) predates the sheet's own LastUpdated stamp (2022-10-11), the 1310 MMcf/d figure appears to be stale relative to when it was recorded, not just outdated now. This is a genuine value disagreement, not a rounding difference (1310 vs 1378 = 5.2% off) — flagging as a spec concern for Update rather than overwriting; two independent origins (operator's current Fast Facts page + FERC/PHMSA regulator dockets) support 1378 MMcf/d as the current correct value.

Second source searched: NGI's 2001-02-26 'It's a Go for $1.6 Billion Gulfstream Pipeline in Florida' independently corroborates the pre-2001 timeline (FERC awarded a preliminary determination 'last April' [April 2000] under docket CP00-6, before Duke/Williams bought the project from Coastal in early 2001) — consistent with, but not an exact-year restatement of, the 1999 proposal date, so this stays medium tier rather than high. No second source explicitly stating '1999' was found in the time available; ProposalMonth left blank (not stated by any source).

verifications.note: PHMSA notice: 'a special permit request from Gulfstream Natural Resources, LLC...to allow an increase in the maximum allowable operating pressure (MAOP) from 2,180 pounds per square inch gauge (psig) to 2,296 psig from Gulfstream Pipeline Mile Post 3.9 to Mile Post 59'
Oil & Gas Journal design feature on the Gulfstream pipeline's compressor-station/pressure design

fills.researcher_notes: 2,180 psig is the baseline/original MAOP that PHMSA's own regulatory record cites for the pipeline (a regulator source, independent of the operator). A subsequent special permit (granted as part of Phase VI, in service July 2022) raised MAOP to 2,296 psig for the offshore Mile Post 3.9-59 segment specifically, with the rest of the line staying at 2,180 psig via pressure-gradient control — i.e. pressure varies by segment on this 745-mile system, so a single sheet-level Pressure value is necessarily an approximation; used the pre-Phase-VI baseline (2180 psig) that applies to most of the route, and noted the segment-specific increase in this entry rather than picking one MP-specific number. Tier held at medium rather than high because the psig figure itself comes from one document (the PHMSA/Federal Register notice); OGJ's design article corroborates the pipeline's unusual single-compressor-station/pressure design generally but was not fully read for a second explicit psig figure in the time available.

summary: P0199 Gulfstream Natural Gas Pipeline: real, correctly-classified, non-duplicate interstate gas line — existence/classification/ownership/StartYear/Length all confirmed high-tier against independent FERC/PHMSA/operator/trade-press sources; two concerns staged (attribution: StartState/Province omits Mississippi, the line's true co-origin; spec: Capacity 1310 MMcf/d looks stale, current operator/FERC data shows 1378 MMcf/d post-2022 Phase VI expansion); 7 MISSING_VALUE fills sourced (Diameter, SegmentCost, Operator high tier; Pressure, Construction medium tier; Proposal medium tier) plus 7 MISSING_REF units given proposed refs, 1 (FuelSource) left UNRESOLVED for lack of a named source facility.
